_description: Timers: clock letters to your queue (tool clock_register), or a program on a clock that adds nothing to your conversation (an on_clock hook). Which to choose: aos/clock.json#/choose.

wake_me._description: Get a message every N cycles in your own queue.

rules._description: When it fires, who can change it, what happens when it cannot send, and the errors.

quiet_timer._description: Run a program every N cycles or ms without anything entering your conversation (hook on_clock).

choose._description: Clock letter, quiet hook, or a hook that tells you only when there is news: what each adds to your history.

wake_me:
# Wake me every N cycles

Call clock_register with op add, a name, every and text; leave out box:
{"op": "add", "name": "check-inbox", "every": 10, "text": "Check data/ for new files."}
Every 10 cycles you get a user message "[aos] clock: cycle 30. Check data/ for new files.". Remove it with {"op": "rm", "name": "check-inbox"}; list with {"op": "ls"}.
To wake another agent, give box = its STACK/queue. Shell: aos-clock-register add --every N --box BOX NAME TEXT.
The register belongs to the clock in $AOS_CLOCK; give daemon D (shell -d D) to use the clock D/clock instead.
rules:
# Clock letters: rules

- It fires when the cycle number divides by every (10, 20, 30 for every 10), not counted from when you added it.
- Anyone who can write the register can add or remove any entry. Remove your entry when you no longer need it; the clock itself only removes entries whose box folder is gone (checked every 100 cycles by default).
- A letter that cannot be sent is only a warning line from the clock; the clock keeps going.
- While you sleep, letters wait in your queue; you get them all when you wake.
- Errors: `EntryExists` (the name is taken: pick another, or `"replace": true`), `EntryMissing` (no entry with that name: `ls` first), `ClockMissing` (no clock: you are not under a daemon tree with one; or give `daemon`), `RegisterBad` (the register file next to the clock cannot be read: a human must fix it), `WriteFailed` (the register cannot be written). Without `box`: `DaemonMissing` / `InstanceMissing` = you are not on a daemon table, so you have no queue to wake; give `box`.
quiet_timer:
# A timer that does not enter your conversation

clock_register letters arrive in your queue, so each one becomes a message. To only run a program on a clock, use a hook instead:
self_hook {"op": "add", "event": "on_clock", "every_ms": 600000, "path": "hooks/check", "on_error": "continue"}
It runs hooks/check when the clock moved 10 minutes' worth of cycles since the last run (checked at the start of each of your steps; once, however many were missed; never while you sleep; it also runs once right after you start, wake up or restart). The program gets clock, cycle, interval_ms, first, last_cycle, missed on stdin. Nothing reaches you unless it sends a letter to your queue (aos-post send STACK/queue). Your definition may have a timer hook (every 5 minutes, does nothing) to replace, and a mail_notify hook (every minute; aos/mailbox.json#/check). How to write the program: aos/me.json#/self_hook/handler.
choose:
# Doing something on a timer: which way

Three ways, told apart by what enters your conversation (history):

1. Clock letter (`clock_register`): a fixed text arrives in your queue every N cycles. Each one is a message in your history and one brain turn, even when there is nothing to do. Use it when you must think every time.
2. `on_clock` hook (`self_hook`): a program runs every N cycles or ms. Nothing enters your history; no brain turn is spent. Use it when a program alone can do the job (copy files, write a log).
3. `on_clock` hook that writes to your queue only when there is news: the program checks something and sends one letter to your queue only then. History grows only then. Example: the stock `mail_notify` hook, on by default (`aos/mailbox.json#/check`).

On an eca body every brain turn costs money: prefer 2 or 3. A message already in your history can be removed with `self_history`. How to write the program: `aos/me.json#/self_hook/handler`.
